terra.problem: God calls Ezekiel “Son of man” once in this passage, not throughout it.
The claims that Nineveh was a big city and Ezekiel was a priest among the exiles come from outside this passage and need references.
The recipe-guessing joke has no connection to the action in the passage, so it does not pass the joke logic test.
The claims about Ezekiel and the exiles being in Babylon, and his delivering the message from far away, require references outside this passage.
The passage mentions high hills among the places of idol worship, but does not say all the high places were hilltop spots or that the sword itself would destroy them.
Calling the high places hilltop spots narrows what the passage says. It mentions high hills, but does not locate every high place on a hilltop.
The passage says the people had idols, but does not say they trusted them.
“Laid waste” means devastated; it does not necessarily mean no structures will remain standing.
The verse says the cities will be laid waste, not that no structures in them will remain standing.
The passage says the survivors will loathe themselves, but does not say they will make no excuses or describe their feeling as sorrow.
The claim about people tearing robes and sitting in ashes elsewhere in the Bible needs a reference.
Ezekiel’s assignment to lie on his side is outside this passage and needs a reference, such as Ezekiel 4:4–6.
The verse identifies these as places where incense was offered to idols; it does not say they were never used as hideouts.
“That’s why the slain lie there” asserts a specific reason for their location that the verse does not state.
